Hmm, okay, backprop always takes me a second to walk through properly. The core trick is that it applies the chain rule, but it does it one layer at a time rather than all at once, which is what makes it tractable. You start at the very end, at the loss, and the gradient flows backward from there through the network, layer after layer. As it moves through each layer, that layer takes whatever gradient it received from the layer after it and multiplies it by its own local derivative, which is just how much that layer's output would change for a tiny change in its input. It's basically the multivariable chain rule applied mechanically, layer by layer, all the way back to the first one. That's the whole idea, once you see it that way it's not so bad.
